summary: Phase 2 of review-flexibility is implemented and verified: the per-dispatch reviewer route override is now reachable through the public workflow apply path. A new review-dispatch submission on the review action carries a human-authorized substitute route into the counter-review dispatch; it is validated exactly like a configured route, recorded on the retained evidence with the human reason, and surfaced in status provenance, without altering the reviewed subject's input fingerprint. The dispatching review offer now honestly advertises the submission kind (absence still tolerated, so every existing no-submission review flow is unchanged); the four reviewing skills document the outage procedure (human-authorized substitute with a required recorded reason; the counter-review is never skipped); archflow-init documents the config overrides section; archflow-upgrade gained the matching one-clause carve-out. Crash-window semantics are request-scoped and pinned by tests: an override lost to an interruption dispatches under the configured route, and a re-submitted override rides the recovered operation identity as a fresh request. One pre-existing type gap found during testing (the status provenance field was untyped for consumers) was closed with a one-line declaration. Verification: typecheck clean; 1165 unit, 502 contract, 221 integration (full suite re-run after the tracked dist rebuild; the pre-rebuild stale-bundle failure is recorded in the transcript), and 34 crash tests all green; offline release check green. Both the server-dispatched counter-review and an independent same-side fresh-context review returned zero findings.
